verses.zh: 参孙到了迦萨，在那里看见一个妓女，就与她亲近。
verses.en: Samson went to Gaza. There he saw a prostitute and slept with her.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “approached her.” The idiom בּוֹא אֶל (boʾ ʾel, “to go to”) is a euphemism for sexual relations.
verses.commentary:
16:1 "Gaza" This was one of five chief cities of the Philistines (i.e., Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Ekron, Gath).
It was 36 miles from Samson's hometown.

▣ "a harlot" The term "harlot" (BDB 275, KB 275, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)
was used of Jephthah's mother in Jdgs. 11:1. Philistine women were Samson's weakness. The Bible presents humans,
warts and all (i.e., 1 Kgs. 11:1-13).

verses.zh: 有人告诉迦萨人说：「参孙到这里来了！」他们就把他团团围住，终夜在城门悄悄埋伏，说：「等到天亮我们便杀他。」
verses.en: The Gazites were told,[NOTE:1] “Samson has come here!” So they surrounded the town[NOTE:2] and hid all night at the city gate, waiting for him to leave.[NOTE:3] They relaxed[NOTE:4] all night, thinking,[NOTE:5] “He will not leave[NOTE:6] until morning comes;[NOTE:7] then we will kill him!”
notes: Heb “To the Gazites, saying.” A verb is missing from the MT; some ancient Greek witnesses add “it was reported.”

Heb “And they surrounded.” The rest of the verse suggests that “the town” is the object, not “the house.” Though the Gazites knew Samson was in the town, apparently they did not know exactly where he had gone. Otherwise, they could have just gone into or surrounded the house and would not have needed to post guards at the city gate.
Heb “and they lay in wait for him all night in the city gate.”
Heb “were silent.”
Heb “saying.”
The words “He will not leave” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “until the light of the morning.”
verses.commentary:
16:2-3 The sequence is uncertain. Apparently the Philistines missed Samson leaving at midnight and did
not even know the gate was gone until the next morning.

Where the Philistines kept watch is not stated but one would assume at the harlot's house or workplace.

verses.zh: 参孙睡到半夜，起来，将城门的门扇、门框、门闩，一齐拆下来，扛在肩上，扛到希伯仑前的山顶上。
verses.en: Samson spent half the night with the prostitute; then he got up in the middle of the night and left.[NOTE:1] He grabbed the doors of the city gate, as well as the two posts, and pulled them right off, bar and all.[NOTE:2] He put them on his shoulders and carried them up to the top of a hill east of Hebron.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And Samson lay until the middle of the night and arose in the middle of the night.”
Heb “with the bar.”
Heb “which is upon the face of Hebron.”
verses.commentary:
16:3 "the city gate. . .carried them to the top of the mountain" This apparently was the smaller wicker door within
the larger city gates. How far Samson carried them is uncertain.

- some think all 36 miles, uphill, to Hebron (Jewish Study Bible)

- others think up the road to Hebron

- the NASB Study Bible thinks as far as Hebron, which was in Judah, as a physical gesture to the Judeans who had
turned him over to the Philistines

verses.zh: 后来，参孙在梭烈谷喜爱一个妇人，名叫大利拉。
verses.en: After this Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in the Sorek Valley.
verses.commentary:
16:4 "Delilah" Her name (BDB 196, KB 222) means:

- "dangling curls" from BDB 195, cf. Song of Songs 7:6, KB 223

- small, slight from KB 223

- "flirtatious" from Arabic root, דלל (IDB, vol. 1, p. 814)

- "night," ‒ word play on Samson's name, "sun"

- "informer" ‒ JB reference edition suggested as a nickname

- "(she who) weakened" ‒ ADJECTIVE "weak," BDB 195

- "devotee" or "worshiper" ‒ James Martin, The Book of Judges, p. 177, The Tyndale OT Commentaries, p. 175

- "traitress" ‒ Jerome Biblical Commentary, p. 160

Obviously it is uncertain from which root it is derived. Josephus (Antiq. 5.8.11) says she was a prostitute
also. It is not specifically stated that she is a Philistine.

verses.zh: 非利士人的首领上去见那妇人，对她说：「求你诓哄参孙，探探他因何有这么大的力气，我们用何法能胜他，捆绑克制他。我们就每人给你一千一百舍客勒银子。」
verses.en: The rulers of the Philistines went up to visit her and said to her, “Trick him! Find out what makes him so strong and how we can subdue him and humiliate[NOTE:1] him. Each one of us will give you 1,100 silver pieces.”
notes: Heb “subdue him in order to humiliate him.”
verses.commentary:
16:5 "The lords of the Philistines" The leaders of the five city-states (NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 295-297) realized
Samson had become a national problem. They were prepared to pay a lot of silver for the information on how to capture him.

▣ "eleven hundred pieces of silver" Delilah may have been a sacred prostitute and this large sum of
money would have mostly gone to the god's temple treasury.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANCIENT NEAR EASTERN WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES

verses.zh: 大利拉对参孙说：「求你告诉我，你因何有这么大的力气，当用何法捆绑克制你。」
verses.en: So Delilah said to Samson, “Tell me what makes you so strong and how you can be subdued and humiliated.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “how you can be subdued in order to be humiliated.”
verses.commentary:
16:6 This question should have made Samson suspicious! It was as if YHWH was blinding his mind to
allow the destruction of all the Philistine leaders (civil and military, Jdgs. 16:27, cf. Jdgs. 14:4).

verses.zh: 参孙回答说：「人若用七条未干的青绳子捆绑我，我就软弱像别人一样。」
verses.en: Samson said to her, “If they tie me up with seven fresh[NOTE:1] bowstrings[NOTE:2] that have not been dried, I will become weak and be just like any other man.”
notes: Or “moist.”
The word refers to a bowstring, probably made from animal tendons. See Ps 11:2; Job 30:11.
verses.commentary:
16:7-18 This series of attacks was accomplished by

- the Philistine military ‒ Jdgs. 16:9

- Delilah herself ‒ Jdgs. 16:12

- Delilah herself ‒ Jdgs. 16:14

- the Philistine military ‒ Jdgs. 16:18

16:7 "seven fresh cords" The RSV has "bowstring," but the term (BDB 452 II, cf. Job 30:11; Ps. 11:2) is uncertain.
This series of tricks implies that the Philistines believed Samson had some magical powers!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #4.

verses.zh: 于是非利士人的首领拿了七条未干的青绳子来，交给妇人，她就用绳子捆绑参孙。
verses.en: So the rulers of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him up with them.

verses.zh: 有人预先埋伏在妇人的内室里。妇人说：「参孙哪，非利士人拿你来了！」参孙就挣断绳子，如挣断经火的麻线一般。这样，他力气的根由人还是不知道。
verses.en: They hid[NOTE:1] in the bedroom and then she said to him, “The Philistines are here,[NOTE:2] Samson!” He snapped the bowstrings as easily as a thread of yarn snaps when it is put close to fire.[NOTE:3] The secret of his strength was not discovered.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “And the ones lying in wait were sitting for her.” The grammatically singular form וְהָאֹרֵב (vehaʾorev) is collective here, referring to the rulers as a group (so also in v. 16).
Heb “are upon you.”
Heb “when it smells fire.”
Heb “His strength was not known.”
verses.commentary: 16:9 "when it touches fire" This same imagery was used in the breaking of the new ropes in Jdgs. 15:14.

verses.zh: 大利拉对参孙说：「你欺哄我，向我说谎言。现在求你告诉我当用何法捆绑你。」
verses.en: Delilah said to Samson, “Look, you deceived[NOTE:1] me and told me lies! Now tell me how you can be subdued.”
notes: See Gen 31:7; Exod 8:29 [8:25 HT]; Job 13:9; Isa 44:20; Jer 9:4 for other uses of this Hebrew word (II תָּלַל, talal), which also occurs in v. 13.
verses.commentary:
16:10 "deceive me" This VERB (BDB 1068, KB 1739, Hiphil PERFECT)
appears in Jdgs. 16:10, 13, 15 and means "trifle with" (i.e., Jer. 9:4; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 298-299).

verses.zh: 参孙回答说：「人若用没有使过的新绳捆绑我，我就软弱像别人一样。」
verses.en: He said to her, “If they tie me tightly with brand new ropes that have never been used,[NOTE:1] I will become weak and be just like any other man.”
notes: Heb “with which no work has been done.”
verses.commentary:
16:11 "bind me tightly" This reflects an intensified construction (i.e., INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE
and IMPERFECT VERB of the same root, BDB 63, KB 75).

verses.zh: 大利拉就用新绳捆绑他，对他说：「参孙哪，非利士人拿你来了！」有人预先埋伏在内室里。参孙将臂上的绳挣断了，如挣断一条线一样。
verses.en: So Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them and said to him, “The Philistines are here,[NOTE:1] Samson!” (The Philistines were hiding in the bedroom.)[NOTE:2] But he tore the ropes[NOTE:3] from his arms as if they were a piece of thread.
notes: Heb “are upon you.”
Heb “And the ones lying in wait were sitting in the bedroom.”
Heb “them”; the referent (the ropes) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 大利拉对参孙说：「你到如今还是欺哄我，向我说谎言。求你告诉我，当用何法捆绑你。」参孙回答说：「你若将我头上的七条发绺，与纬线同织就可以了。」
verses.en: Delilah said to Samson, “Up to now you have deceived me and told me lies. Tell me how you can be subdued.” He said to her, “If you weave the seven braids of my hair[NOTE:1] into the fabric on the loom[NOTE:2] and secure it with the pin, I will become weak and be like any other man.”
notes: Heb “head” (also in the following verse). By metonymy the head is mentioned in the Hebrew text in place of the hair on it.
Heb “with the web.” For a discussion of how Delilah did this, see C. F. Burney, Judges, 381, and G. F. Moore, Judges (ICC), 353-54.
verses.commentary: 16:13-14 Notice that the NASB shows the textual expansion by adding parenthetical brackets.

verses.zh: 于是大利拉将他的发绺与纬线同织，用橛子钉住，对他说：「参孙哪，非利士人拿你来了！」参孙从睡中醒来，将机上的橛子和纬线一齐都拔出来了。
verses.en: So she made him go to sleep, wove the seven braids of his hair into the fabric on the loom, fastened it with the pin, and said to him, “The Philistines are here,[NOTE:1] Samson!”[NOTE:2] He woke up[NOTE:3] and tore away the pin of the loom and the fabric.
notes: Heb “are upon you.”

The MT of vv. 13b-14a reads simply, “He said to her, ‘If you weave the seven braids of my head with the web.’ And she fastened with the pin and said to him.” The additional words in the translation, “and secure it with the pin, I will become weak and be like any other man.’ 16:14 So she made him go to sleep, wove the seven braids of his hair into the fabric on the loom,” which without doubt represent the original text, are supplied from the ancient Greek version. (In both vv. 13b and 14a the Greek version has “to the wall” after “with the pin,” but this is an interpretive addition that reflects a misunderstanding of ancient weaving equipment. See G. F. Moore, Judges [ICC], 353-54.) The Hebrew textual tradition was accidentally shortened during the copying process. A scribe’s eye jumped from the first instance of “with the web” to the second, causing him to leave out inadvertently the intervening words.
The Hebrew adds, “from his sleep.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary: 16:14 Samson fled with his hair attached to the loom!

verses.zh: 大利拉对参孙说：「你既不与我同心，怎么说你爱我呢？你这三次欺哄我，没有告诉我，你因何有这么大的力气。」
verses.en: She said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when you will not share your secret with me?[NOTE:1] Three times you have deceived me and have not told me what makes you so strong.”
notes: Heb “when your heart is not with me.”

verses.zh: 大利拉天天用话催逼他，甚至他心里烦闷要死。
verses.en: She nagged him[NOTE:1] every day and pressured him until he was sick to death of it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “forced him with her words.”
Heb “and his spirit was short [i.e., impatient] to the point of death.”
verses.commentary:
16:16 "she pressed him daily with her words. . .soul was annoyed to death" This same thing happened
in Jdgs. 14:17, but is expressed by a different Hebrew word.

verses.zh: 参孙就把心中所藏的都告诉了她，对她说：「向来人没有用剃头刀剃我的头，因为我自出母胎就归　神作拿细耳人；若剃了我的头发，我的力气就离开我，我便软弱像别人一样。」
verses.en: Finally he told her his secret.[NOTE:1] He said to her, “My hair has never been cut,[NOTE:2] for I have been dedicated to God[NOTE:3] from the time I was conceived.[NOTE:4] If my head[NOTE:5] were shaved, my strength would leave me; I would become weak and be just like all other men.”
notes: Heb “all his heart.”
Heb “a razor has not come upon my head.”
Or “set apart to God.” Traditionally the Hebrew term נָזִיר (nazir) has been translated “Nazirite.” The word is derived from the verb נָזַר (nazar, “to dedicate; to consecrate; to set apart”).
Heb “from the womb of my mother.”
Heb “I.” The referent has been made more specific in the translation (“my head”).
verses.commentary:
16:17 "a Nazirite to God" Samson knew the angel's message! He had violated every aspect except the
hair (cf. Numbers 6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAZIRITE VOW

verses.zh: 大利拉见他把心中所藏的都告诉了她，就打发人到非利士人的首领那里，对他们说：「他已经把心中所藏的都告诉了我，请你们再上来一次。」于是非利士人的首领手里拿着银子，上到妇人那里。
verses.en: When Delilah saw that he had told her his secret,[NOTE:1] she sent for[NOTE:2] the rulers of the Philistines, saying, “Come up here again, for he has told me[NOTE:3] his secret.”[NOTE:4] So the rulers of the Philistines went up to visit her, bringing the silver in their hands.
notes: Heb “all his heart.”
Heb “she sent and summoned.”
The translation follows the Qere, לִי (li, “to me”) rather than the Kethib, לָהּ (lah, “to her”).
Heb “all his heart.”
verses.commentary: 16:18 "Come up once more" See Jdgs. 16:8-9.

verses.zh: 大利拉使参孙枕着她的膝睡觉，叫了一个人来剃除他头上的七条发绺。于是大利拉克制他，他的力气就离开他了。
verses.en: She made him go to sleep on her lap[NOTE:1] and then called a man in to shave off[NOTE:2] the seven braids of his hair.[NOTE:3] She made him vulnerable[NOTE:4] and his strength left him.
notes: Heb “on her knees.” The expression is probably euphemistic for sexual intercourse. See HALOT 160-61 s.v. בֶּרֶךְ.
Heb “she called for a man and she shaved off.” The point seems to be that Delilah acted through the instrumentality of the man. See J. A. Soggin, Judges (OTL), 254.
Heb “head.” By metonymy the hair of his head is meant.

Heb “She began to humiliate him.” Rather than referring to some specific insulting action on Delilah’s part after Samson’s hair was shaved off, this statement probably means that she, through the devious actions just described, began the process of Samson’s humiliation which culminates in the following verses.
verses.commentary:
16:19 "She made him sleep on her knees" I think Samson was really fooled into thinking that she cared
about him. How sad! The NET Bible suggests it is an idiom or euphemism for intercourse.

▣ "seven locks of his hair" The hair was not magical but represented his dedication to God's use.

▣ "she began to afflict him" I think this refers to her shouting, "the Philistines are upon you" (cf. Jdgs.
16:9, 12, 14, 20).

verses.zh: 大利拉说：「参孙哪，非利士人拿你来了！」参孙从睡中醒来，心里说：「我要像前几次出去活动身体」；他却不知道耶和华已经离开他了。
verses.en: She said, “The Philistines are here,[NOTE:1] Samson!” He woke up[NOTE:2] and thought,[NOTE:3] “I will do as I did before[NOTE:4] and shake myself free.” But he did not realize that the Lord had left him.
notes: Heb “are upon you.”
The Hebrew adds, “from his sleep.” This has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “and said.”
Heb “I will go out as before.”
verses.commentary:
16:20 "but he did not know that the Lord had departed from him" What a tragedy!
But it is true when there is no emphasis on personal relationship and commitment.

verses.zh: 非利士人将他拿住，剜了他的眼睛，带他下到迦萨，用铜链拘索他；他就在监里推磨。
verses.en: The Philistines captured him and gouged out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza and bound him in bronze chains. He became a grinder in the prison.
verses.commentary:
16:21 "gouged out his eyes" This was a common practice in the ANE.

▣ "with bronze chains" These chains (BDB 639, #2) refer to copper or bronze chains (cf. 2 Sam. 3:34;
2 Kgs. 25:7; 2 Chr. 33:11; 36:6; Jer. 39:7; 52:11; Lam. 3:7).

▣ "he was a grinder in the prison" This was apparently a hand grinder. The humiliation was that it was
a slave's (cf. Job 31:10) or a woman's task.

verses.zh: 然而他的头发被剃之后，又渐渐长起来了。
verses.en: His hair[NOTE:1] began to grow back after it had been shaved off.
notes: Heb “the hair of his head.”

verses.zh: 非利士人的首领聚集，要给他们的神大衮献大祭，并且欢乐，因为他们说：「我们的神将我们的仇敌参孙交在我们手中了。」
verses.en: The rulers of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to celebrate. They said, “Our god has handed Samson, our enemy, over to us.”
verses.commentary:
16:23 "Dagon" This was a grain god (ABD, p. 2) of the Fertile Crescent (BDB 186) from the third millennium. The
Philistines assimilated the religious culture of the Canaanites (cf. Jos. 15:41; 19:27; 1 Samuel 5; 1 Chr. 10:10). In some texts
found at Ugarit, Dagon is the father of Ba'al.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANCIENT NEAR EAST

verses.zh: 众人看见参孙，就赞美他们的神说：「我们的神将毁坏我们地、杀害我们许多人的仇敌交在我们手中了。」
verses.en: When the people saw him,[NOTE:1] they praised their god, saying, “Our god has handed our enemy over to us, the one who ruined our land and killed so many of us!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Most interpret this as a reference to Samson, but this seems premature, since v. 25 suggests he was not yet standing before them. Consequently some prefer to see this statement as displaced and move it to v. 25 (see C. F. Burney, Judges, 387). It seems more likely that the pronoun refers to an image of Dagon.
Heb “multiplied our dead.”

verses.zh: 他们正宴乐的时候，就说：「叫参孙来，在我们面前戏耍戏耍。」于是将参孙从监里提出来，他就在众人面前戏耍。他们使他站在两柱中间。
verses.en: When they really started celebrating,[NOTE:1] they said, “Call for Samson so he can entertain us!” So they summoned Samson from the prison and he entertained them.[NOTE:2] They made him stand between two pillars.
notes: Heb “When their heart was good.”
Heb “before them.”
verses.commentary:
16:25 "they were in high spirits" They were drunk.

▣ "he entertained them" It is uncertain as to how he entertained them, but it had to be humiliating to Samson.

verses.zh: 参孙向拉他手的童子说：「求你让我摸着托房的柱子，我要靠一靠。」
verses.en: Samson said to the young man who held his hand, “Position me so I can touch the pillars that support the temple.[NOTE:1] Then I can lean on them.”
notes: Heb “the pillars upon which the house is founded.”
verses.commentary: 16:26 "Let me feel the pillars" He pretended to need to rest.

verses.zh: 那时房内充满男女，非利士人的众首领也都在那里。房的平顶上约有三千男女观看参孙戏耍。
verses.en: Now the temple[NOTE:1] was filled with men and women, and all the rulers of the Philistines were there. There were 3,000 men and women on the roof watching Samson entertain.
notes: Heb “house.”
verses.commentary:
16:27 "about 3,000. . .on the roof" The structure of this temple was common in this day. There are many
archaeological examples. The dignitaries were seated under the roof and the populous were on the roof. Several
wooden pillars provided support.

verses.zh: 参孙求告耶和华说：「主耶和华啊，求你眷念我。　神啊，求你赐我这一次的力量，使我在非利士人身上报那剜我双眼的仇。」
verses.en: Samson called to the Lord, “O Sovereign Lord,[NOTE:1] remember me! Strengthen me just one more time, O God, so I can get swift revenge[NOTE:2] against the Philistines for my two eyes!”
notes: The Hebrew has אֲדֹנָי יֱהֹוִה (ʾadonay yehovih, “Lord Yahweh”).
Heb “so I can get revenge with one act of vengeance.”
verses.commentary:
16:28 "Lord. . .Lord. . .God" YHWH. . .
Adonai. . .Elohim.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (kurios)

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What was the purpose of Samson's "ministry" to Israel?

- Was Samson's hair the source or symbol of his strength?

- How could the Spirit leave him and he not know it?

- How does Jdgs. 16:28 relate to Jdgs. 14:4?

- Why are there concluding statements at both Jdgs. 15:20 and 16:31?

verses.zh: 参孙就抱住托房的那两根柱子：左手抱一根，右手抱一根，
verses.en: Samson took hold of the two middle pillars that supported the temple[NOTE:1] and he leaned against them, with his right hand on one and his left hand on the other.
notes: Heb “the pillars upon which the house was founded.”

verses.zh: 说：「我情愿与非利士人同死！」就尽力屈身，房子倒塌，压住首领和房内的众人。这样，参孙死时所杀的人比活着所杀的还多。
verses.en: Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed hard,[NOTE:1] and the temple collapsed on the rulers and all the people in it. He killed many more people in his death than he had killed during his life.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he stretched out with strength.”
Heb “And the ones whom he killed in his death were many more than he killed in his life.”

verses.zh: 参孙的弟兄和他父的全家都下去取他的尸首，抬上来葬在琐拉和以实陶中间，在他父玛挪亚的坟墓里。参孙作以色列的士师二十年。
verses.en: His brothers and all his family[NOTE:1] went down and brought him back.[NOTE:2] They buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had led[NOTE:3] Israel for 20 years.
notes: Heb “and all the house of his father.”
Heb “and lifted him up and brought up.”
Traditionally, “judged.”

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This may be an additional account added later (cf. Jdgs. 15:20). See John H. Walton and D. Brent Sandy,
The Lost World of Scripture.

- Samson's weakness was his lust for Philistine women.

- girl from Timnah, Judges 14

- harlot from Gaza, Jdgs. 16:1-3

- seductress from the Sorek valley, Jdgs. 16:4-31

- Samson seems so naive in his dealings with Delilah. His love made him blind and so did the Philistine leaders!
What a tragedy. However, Jdgs. 14:4 looms in the background!
